```{r}

n_periph = length( prevalence [prevalence< periph_thresh & prevalence> 0.00001]) # some species have prevalance of 0 after threshold filtering

n_sub_core =  length( prevalence [prevalence > sub_core_thresh & prevalence < core_thresh] )
```

```{r}

  annotate(geom='label', x=0.85, y=6.0, label= paste("Core > 97%", n_core), size=5) + #0001:3.2

        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),      # Remove major grid lines
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load and Prepare Data ---

# Read data from the two CSV files
# Make sure "one.csv" and "two.csv" are in your working directory or provide the correct path

data1 <- read.csv("../results/microbial_signatures/001/Chennai_species_prevalence.csv")
data2 <- read.csv("../results/microbial_signatures/001/core_species_prevalence.csv")

# Create separate data frames with an identifier for each dataset
prev1 <- data.frame(prevalence = data1$prevalence, dataset = "Chennai")
prev2 <- data.frame(prevalence = data2$prevalence, dataset = "MetaSUB")

# Combine the two data frames into one
combined_data <- rbind(prev1, prev2)

# Define the prevalence thresholds
core_thresh <- 0.97
sub_core_thresh <- 0.8
periph_thresh <- 0.15

# --- 2. Create the Plot ---

# Create the ggplot object using the combined data
# Map the 'dataset' column to the fill and color aesthetics
plot <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = prevalence, fill = dataset, color = dataset)) +
  # Add two density layers with transparency (alpha) to see the overlap
  geom_density(size = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Set custom colors for the plots
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Chennai" = "lightblue", "MetaSUB" = "#FFB6C1")) + # lightblue and lightpink
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Chennai" = "darkblue", "MetaSUB" = "darkred")) +
  
  # Apply a minimal theme and set labels
  theme_minimal() +
  xlab('Species Prevalence') +
  ylab('Density') +
  labs(title = "Superimposed Density of Species Prevalence") +
  
  # Customize theme elements
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(), # Remove major grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), # Remove minor grid lines
    legend.position = "top" # Position the legend at the top
  )

# --- 3. Display and Save the Plot ---

# Print the plot to the RStudio plot pane
print(plot)

# Save the plot to a file
# The file will be saved in a subfolder named 'figures'. Make sure it exists.
if (!dir.exists("figures")) {
  dir.create("figures")
}
ggsave("../figures/Figure_Superimposed_Density.png", plot = plot, dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 5)

```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load and Prepare Data ---

# Read data from the two CSV files
# Ensure the file paths are correct
data2 <- read.csv("../results/microbial_signatures/001/core_species_prevalence_all.csv")
```

```{r}
# Define the filtering thresholds to iterate over.
# These represent the minimum fraction of cities a species must be present in.
filtering_thresholds <- c(0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75)

# Define the constant prevalence thresholds for the vertical indicator lines on the plot
core_thresh <- 0.97
sub_core_thresh <- 0.8
periph_thresh <- 0.15


output_dir <- "../figures"

# --- 2. Pre-computation ---

# Identify city columns (all columns except 'Species')
city_cols <- setdiff(names(data2), "Species")
num_cities <- length(city_cols)

# Calculate the 'presence ratio' for each species
# This is the fraction of cities where the species is present (not NA).
if (num_cities > 0) {
    data2$presence_ratio <- rowSums(!is.na(data2[city_cols])) / num_cities
} else {
    stop("Error: No city columns found. The CSV must have columns for cities besides the 'Species' column.")
}


# --- 3. Loop, Filter, Plot, and Save ---

# Loop over each defined threshold
for (current_threshold in filtering_thresholds) {

  # Filter the data: keep species with a 'presence_ratio' greater than or equal to the current threshold
  filtered_data <- data2 %>%
    filter(presence_ratio >= current_threshold)

  # If no data remains after filtering, print a message and skip to the next threshold
  if (nrow(filtered_data) == 0) {
    message(paste("No species found for presence ratio >=", current_threshold, ". Skipping plot generation."))
    next
  }

  # --- Calculate Median Prevalence for Plotting ---
  # For the remaining species, calculate the median of their prevalence values across all cities.
  # The 'apply' function works row-by-row (MARGIN = 1). 'na.rm = TRUE' is crucial to ignore NAs.
  median_prevalence <- apply(filtered_data[city_cols], 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

  # Prepare the final data for plotting
  plot_data <- data.frame(prevalence = median_prevalence, dataset = "MetaSUB")

  # --- Create the Plot ---
  plot_title <- paste0("Density of Median Species Prevalence (Presence Ratio >= ", current_threshold, ")")

  current_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = prevalence)) +
    geom_density(fill = "#FFB6C1", color = "darkred", size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
    
    # Apply a minimal theme and set labels
    theme_minimal() +
    xlab('Median Species Prevalence') +
    ylab('Normalized Density') +
    labs(title = plot_title) +
    
    # Customize theme elements for a cleaner look
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
      panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )

  # --- Save the Plot ---
  # Generate a unique filename for each plot based on its threshold
  file_name <- sprintf("Figure_Density_Median_Prevalence_Ratio_%.2f.png", current_threshold)
  output_path <- file.path(output_dir, file_name)

  ggsave(output_path, plot = current_plot, dpi = 600, width = 8, height = 5)

  message(paste("Successfully saved plot to:", output_path))
}

message("Script finished. All plots have been generated.")

```

```{r}
# --- 1. Load Libraries ---
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 2. Define Constants and File Paths ---
# NOTE: Ensure these file paths are correct for your system.
chennai_file_path <- "../results/microbial_signatures/001/Chennai_species_prevalence.csv"
metasub_file_path <- "../results/microbial_signatures/001/core_species_prevalence_all.csv"

# Prevalence thresholds for vertical lines and annotations
core_thresh <- 0.97
sub_core_thresh <- 0.8
periph_thresh <- 0.15

# Filtering threshold for the MetaSUB dataset
metasub_presence_threshold <- 0.5

# --- 3. Process Dataset 1 (Chennai) ---
chennai_data <- read_csv(chennai_file_path)

# Calculate counts for annotations (based on Chennai data)
n_periph <- sum(chennai_data$prevalence < periph_thresh & chennai_data$prevalence > 0)
n_core <- sum(chennai_data$prevalence > core_thresh)
n_sub_core <- sum(chennai_data$prevalence > sub_core_thresh & chennai_data$prevalence < core_thresh)

# Prepare the data frame for plotting, adding a source column
plot_data_chennai <- data.frame(
  prevalence = chennai_data$prevalence,
  source = "Chennai"
)

# --- 4. Process Dataset 2 (MetaSUB) ---
metasub_data <- read_csv(metasub_file_path)

# Identify city columns and calculate presence ratio
city_cols <- setdiff(names(metasub_data), "Species")
num_cities <- length(city_cols)
metasub_data$presence_ratio <- rowSums(!is.na(metasub_data[city_cols])) / num_cities

# Filter data based on presence ratio
filtered_metasub <- metasub_data %>%
  filter(presence_ratio >= metasub_presence_threshold)

# Calculate the median prevalence for the filtered species
median_prevalence <- apply(filtered_metasub[city_cols], 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

# Prepare the data frame for plotting, adding a source column
plot_data_metasub <- data.frame(
  prevalence = median_prevalence,
  source = "MetaSUB"
)

# --- 5. Combine Data ---
combined_data <- rbind(plot_data_chennai, plot_data_metasub)

# --- 6. Create the Superimposed Plot ---
superimposed_plot <- ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = prevalence, fill = source, color = source)) +
  # Add density layers with transparency
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  
  # Add vertical lines for thresholds
  geom_vline(xintercept = periph_thresh, color = 'black', linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sub_core_thresh, color = 'black', linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = core_thresh, color = 'black', linetype = "dashed") +
  
  # Add annotations (note: counts are from Chennai data)
  annotate(geom = 'label', x = 0.6, y = 2.4, label = paste("Sub-Core 80-97%:", n_sub_core), size = 4) +
  annotate(geom = 'label', x = 0.15, y = 6.0, label = paste("Peripheral < 15%:", n_periph), size = 4) +
  annotate(geom = 'label', x = 0.9, y = 6.0, label = paste("Core > 97%:", n_core), size = 4) +
  
  # Manually set the colors to match your original plots
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Chennai" = "lightblue", "MetaSUB" = "#FFB6C1")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Chennai" = "darkblue", "MetaSUB" = "darkred")) +
  
  # Apply theme and labels
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Species Prevalence",
    x = "Species Prevalence",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Dataset", # Legend title for fill
    color = "Dataset"    # Legend title for color
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

# --- 7. Display and Save the Plot ---
print(superimposed_plot)

ggsave(
  "../figures/Figure_2_Superimposed.png",
  plot = superimposed_plot,
  dpi = 600,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)
ggsave(

  "../figures/Figure_2_Superimposed.pdf",
  plot = superimposed_plot,
  dpi = 600,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
)
```
